bullets.title: Kimi K3 AI breakthrough triggers semiconductor selloff — DeepSeek déjà vu
bullets.body: Chinese startup Moonshot's Kimi K3 model is being cited as rivaling OpenAI and Anthropic, sparking a broad chipmaker selloff with market participants explicitly drawing parallels to last year's DeepSeek shock. Semiconductor index approaching bear market threshold at near -20% drawdown. High-beta stocks are down more than 20%, on track for their worst month since the 2008 Global Financial Crisis.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO pushes back on chip delay narrative; Japan AI factory live with 27,500 Rubin GPUs
bullets.body: Jensen Huang directly refuted the 'chip delay' narrative, asserting that 'giant amounts' of Vera Rubin GPUs are coming to market. Japan's first AI factory is operational with 27,500 Rubin units deployed. The pushback comes as CNBC is seen by some traders as reversing its prior 'chips to infinity' narrative.

bullets.title: Apple overtakes Nvidia as world's most valuable company at $4.92T
bullets.body: AAPL surpassed NVDA in early trading Friday, reaching a $4.92 trillion market cap versus NVDA's $4.86 trillion, reclaiming the top spot amid the semiconductor selloff.

bullets.title: META hiring senior AWS exec Dave Brown to lead cloud infrastructure push
bullets.body: Meta is poaching Dave Brown, one of AWS's most senior executives with nearly two decades at Amazon, to lead its infrastructure group as the company weighs entering cloud services. Brown will report to META's head of infrastructure.

bullets.title: MRVL Buy maintained; F2Q27E +12% QoQ rev, margins beat Street
bullets.body: Analyst maintains MRVL at Buy with $280 price target, modeling F2Q27 revenue +12% QoQ with ~59% non-GAAP gross margin vs. Street's 58.8%, and F3Q27 at +13% QoQ vs. consensus +11%. QCOM initiated at Hold. Memory/storage names MU and SNDK weak pre-market while SKHY resilient.

bullets.title: K3-type models compress frontier AI margins but benefit cloud/infra providers
bullets.body: Analyst commentary argues K3-style efficient models are structurally bad for frontier AI company margins (including Claude Opus) but benefit cloud, TaaS, and infrastructure providers. Moonshot itself is characterized as supply-constrained. Chinese labs can freely rent GPUs outside China, undermining export control effectiveness.

bullets.title: Netflix Q2 revenue $12.6B (+13.5% YoY); analyst PTs cut post-print
bullets.body: Netflix reported Q2 revenue of $12.6B, up from $11.1B a year ago (+13.5% YoY). Post-print, Morgan Stanley cut its PT to $83 from $90 and Bernstein cut to $95 from $100.

bullets.title: Momentum trade crashing; hedge funds still too long Japan and Nasdaq
bullets.body: Hedgeye's macro strategist warns that 'widely-held momentum trades are crashing' and that breaking immediate-term support triggers algorithmic selling cascades. Separately noted: hedge funds remain significantly overweight both Japan and NASDAQ-100 exposure. QQQ is testing the lower end of its alpha code support.

bullets.title: Broad market breadth divergence: 74% of stocks up, but not mega-cap momentum names
bullets.body: Despite 9 of 11 sectors rising and 74% of stocks averaging +2.4% gains on Thursday, the CNBC retail investor portfolio has round-tripped to flat in 2026 as mega-cap momentum names drive the divergence. Mag-7 stocks are described as the 'last support' for broader indexes.

bullets.title: Global market selloff: Nikkei -4% (drawdown -11.4%), Shanghai -3.1%
bullets.body: Japanese stocks fell another 4.0% Friday, bringing the Nikkei's drawdown to -11.4% from its cycle peak. Shanghai equities dropped 3.1% and remain in a bearish trend. Nasdaq volatility heading toward the 'F-bucket' — historically elevated levels.

bullets.title: Earnings quality concern: accounting earnings healthy but cash generation weakening
bullets.body: The MarketEar flags that while accounting earnings continue to look healthy, cash generation is deteriorating relative to reported earnings, raising potential earnings quality issues heading into results season.

bullets.title: SEC reportedly moving toward eliminating mandatory quarterly earnings reporting
bullets.body: The SEC is said to be likely to move forward with its proposal to eliminate the requirement for public companies to report earnings four times annually, with no clear replacement framework yet detailed.

bullets.title: Geopolitical escalation: Iran attacks Kuwait power/water plant; IRGC threatens stronger retaliation
bullets.body: Iran's IRGC claims to have attacked the U.S. Al Udeid base in Qatar and struck Kuwait's water desalination and power plant. Iran is also calling on Gulf neighbors to block use of their territory for attacks, with the IRGC warning that any further strikes on Iran will result in stronger retaliation. Hormuz strait crossings hit a 3-week low with just 8 confirmed on July 16.

bullets.title: Data center power constraints flagged at World AI Conference; renewable alignment required
bullets.body: The 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference statement explicitly identified power availability as a binding constraint for data center expansion, recommending that large compute clusters be located in regions with abundant renewable energy. Xi Jinping delivered the keynote. NVDA, MU, SNDK, and LITE were referenced in the context of the conference.

bullets.title: Optical networking dominates data center scale-out; NVDA NVLink copper still rules scale-up
bullets.body: Commentary notes optical networking is already widely deployed for cross-datacenter scale-out connections, but low-latency GPU-to-GPU scale-up within racks still relies primarily on copper technologies like NVIDIA NVLink. Copper faces increasing challenges as signaling speeds rise.

bullets.title: Michael Burry sees 'bargain hunting' opportunity in Hong Kong stocks as Korea shine fades
bullets.body: Michael Burry suggested it is worth trying to go 'bargain hunting' in Hong Kong's market, noting that Hong Kong lagged peers in the global AI rally this year and that he expects the shine to come off Korea.

bullets.title: US retail spending missed expectations despite World Cup tourism and online sales events
bullets.body: US retail sales came in weaker than expected last month, with the World Cup drawing international tourists and online sales events failing to offset consumer softness. Labor market slack is now reportedly exceeding levels seen during the Global Financial Crisis.

bullets.title: WTI crude showing bullish immediate-term momentum; oil tanker struck near Black Sea CPC terminal
bullets.body: Hedgeye's alpha code flags WTI crude in bullish immediate-term TRADE momentum. Separately, an oil tanker was struck near the CPC terminal in the Black Sea, adding to geopolitical risk in energy shipping.

bullets.title: BOJ likely to raise growth forecast; signals no urgency for back-to-back rate hikes
bullets.body: Sources indicate the BOJ is likely to raise its growth forecast for the year but sees little need for consecutive rate hikes, suggesting a measured approach to policy normalization even as the Nikkei suffers a significant drawdown.

bullets.title: High systemic leverage poses amplified downside risk if sentiment reverses
bullets.body: Commentary flags that leverage is available across markets and 'everywhere you turn some form of leverage is on.' The buildup is described as creating larger downside risks in any market reversal, with the author noting it is 'hard to know the limits of leverage in the current environment.'
